common_name: Unidentified: dying strappy plant with one new leaf
id_basis: Dead strappy, striped leaves and one new green oval leaf at the centre. Not enough to identify.

From the October 21 close-ups. The new leaf is glossy, lance-shaped with a pointed tip and a clear midrib, and has a small swollen joint (a geniculum) where the blade meets the stalk, which peace lilies have. The leaf stalks are sheathing and come straight up from the soil in a clump of several crowns, with papery brown sheaths around the new shoots. The dead leaves shrivelled lengthwise into narrow tan strips, which is how peace lily leaves dry out; that is why they looked strappy before. Several green shoots are coming up from the base, so the roots are alive.

temp_notes: Peace lilies sulk below 55°F and leaves are damaged below about 45-50°F. Keep it above 60°F while it regrows. Heat above 90°F is fine in shade if it stays watered.
humidity_notes: Prefers 50% or more but grows well in normal indoor air of 40%. Very dry air gives brown leaf tips.
light_summary: Bright indirect light; tolerates shade. No direct afternoon sun.
light_notes: An east window or a few feet back from a south or west window. Direct sun scorches the leaves; deep shade means few or no flowers.
winter_summary: Bring it inside before nights reach 50°F. Indoors it can keep growing in a warm, bright room.
health_summary: Nearly all foliage is dead; one healthy new leaf at the centre.
Recovering. Almost all the old leaves are dead, but one healthy new leaf has opened and several green shoots are coming up from the crowns.

health_steps:
Check the roots: firm and white is OK, brown and mushy is rot
Cut off the dead leaves
Empty the saucer
Keep warm and lightly moist

Cut the dead leaves off near the soil with clean scissors. Leave the papery sheaths that wrap the new shoots.
Water when the top inch of mix feels dry, then empty the saucer. Do not keep it soggy while it has so few leaves.
Keep it warm (above 60°F) and in bright, indirect light.
No fertilizer until it has three or four new leaves, then half strength.
Do not repot until it is growing well; then move it to fresh mix only one size up.
water_notes: Unknown species. Water when the top inch of mix is dry, soak, and empty the saucer. Adjust once the plant is identified.

Water when the top inch (2-3 cm) of mix is dry. A peace lily droops clearly when thirsty and perks up within hours of watering, but do not wait for that every time. Empty the saucer. With few leaves it uses little water, so check before watering.
soil_medium: General well-draining potting mix with about 20% perlite. Adjust once the plant is identified.
Rich, moisture-holding but well-draining mix: about 60% potting soil, 20% perlite and 20% orchid bark or coir. Drainage holes are essential.
fertilizer: Balanced liquid, such as 20-20-20, at quarter to half strength
nutrients: Feed lightly (half strength) every 4 weeks in spring and summer, and not in winter, until the plant is identified.
Feed every 6 weeks from April to September at half strength, only once it is growing again. Peace lilies are light feeders; too much fertilizer burns the leaf tips.
